clue.text: Extravagant spending, as you'd expect from over-the-top diva playing Mimi?

definitions.meaning: lavish showy buying meant to display wealth

definitions.text: as you'd expect from over-the-top diva playing Mimi?
definitions.meaning: an overacting soprano is hard to miss, and Mimi in Puccini's La Bohème dies of tuberculosis, once called by that wasting-disease name

explanation.surface: A remark about an opera star hamming up her role as the heroine of La Bohème.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a showy diva is noticeable, and Mimi's illness in La Bohème is the old name for tuberculosis.
explanation.definitionFit: The economist Veblen's term for buying luxuries chiefly to display wealth is this exact phrase.

clue.text: Initially inferior count: sceptical, sadly, about making a baby?

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters before it are jumbled
initially takes just the opening letter of the word inferior

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doubtful nobleman is gloomy about the prospect of fathering an heir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about making a baby?' plays on conception: the answer, really meaning concerned with concepts, is read as if it described conceiving.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful reading: conception is making a baby, so an adjective built on concept is jokingly taken as relating to that.

clue.text: Dignified refusal to live without Lord's lead

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the verb's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter, here from Lord's

explanation.surface: A stately person declines to carry on living without a nobleman to guide them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'lead' takes the first letter of Lord's.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes bearing that is lofty and dignified, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Entry of Gladiators ultimately in old man's time

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man, so old man's gives PA'S
an age is a period of time

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Gladiators

explanation.surface: The arrival of gladiators into the arena during a father's era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives S, the last letter of Gladiators, which goes 'in' PA'S AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a way in or through, so it is an entry in the sense of an entrance.

clue.text: Peach that's ready to be pulled

definitions.meaning: a peach is something or someone excellent or very attractive
a Christmas novelty tube with a snap inside that two people pull apart

explanation.surface: A ripe fruit waiting to be plucked from the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' looks like the fruit, but it means a stunner; the second half is the Christmas paper tube that bangs when two people tug it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British slang and custom: a stunning person, and the festive tube pulled at Christmas dinner.

clue.text: A film on sea paintings by Hammer?

parts.note: oils are paintings done in oil paint
to lick is to beat or thrash, as to hammer is

explanation.surface: A Hammer horror movie set at sea, illustrated with artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' and 'Hammer' suggest the British horror studio, but the film is a coating, and hammer means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of spilt crude floating on the water is literally a thin film on the sea.

clue.text: Film musical with tempestuous shower scene ended by a cop

definitions.text: Film musical with tempestuous shower scene ended by a cop

parts.words: Film musical with tempestuous shower scene ended by a cop
parts.note: the famous 1952 Gene Kelly number danced in a downpour, which stops when a policeman looks on

explanation.surface: A movie musical with a stormy bathroom scene interrupted by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower scene' suggests Psycho, but the shower is rain in the famous 1952 song-and-dance number, cut short when a policeman appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The description matches the celebrated MGM musical whose title number Gene Kelly dances in a downpour.

clue.text: Tasty-looking Estuary drink in glass girl put aside

parts.note: a river's mouth is its estuary
water is a drink
taken as written

indicators.note: put aside means the named part is removed from the word before

parts.note: lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl sets down her glass of something delicious by a river estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put aside' removes LASS from GLASS, leaving G; 'Estuary' hints at Estuary English but is just a river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Food so appealing it makes saliva flow is described as appetising or tasty-looking.

clue.text: Such as the Guardian making southern English town assume importance

parts.note: Reading is a large town in Berkshire, west of London
to matter is to be important

explanation.surface: The newspaper making a Berkshire town feel significant.
explanation.walkthrough: READING is a town in Berkshire in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper like the Guardian is an example of material for people to read.

clue.text: Number 10, perhaps, in full, is including everything

definitions.meaning: a number 10 is a bus route, and bus is short for the longer old word
comprehensive, covering many items in one collection

explanation.surface: Downing Street, at full strength, takes in every matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' suggests Downing Street, but it is a bus route; the full form of bus is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bus is a clipping of this Latin word, and as an adjective it means comprehensive, as in an edition of collected works.

clue.text: Crestfallen Democrats covering up president no longer

indicators.note: covering up means the letters are concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Dejected Democrats concealing a former president's misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering up' hides ALLENDE across crestfALLEN DEmocrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Allende was president of Chile until his death in the 1973 coup.

clue.text: Could be Disneyland's crafty means of saving the species, Euro-politician included

indicators.note: included means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.words: crafty means of saving the species
parts.note: Noah's ark, a craft, saved the species from the Flood
an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament

explanation.surface: Disney's cunning conservation plan, with a Brussels politician on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' is a pun on craft, a vessel: Noah's boat saved the species, and the Euro-politician is 'included' between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Disneyland is a famous example of an amusement park built around a theme.

clue.text: Landowner, look, into line dancing at first

indicators.note: into places one piece inside another
at first takes the opening letter of each of line and dancing

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A landowner is told to look into line dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' is not LO but AIR, an appearance; it goes 'into' L and D, the first letters of line and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a laird is the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Supporting comedian Henry

parts.note: a wit is a funny person
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Backing the comic Lenny Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comedian Henry' suggests Lenny Henry, but it is WIT plus H, the symbol of the henry unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To be with someone is to be on their side, supporting them.

clue.text: Ray's getting turned away, sadly, for certain

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone named Ray is definitely being sent away, regrettably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man being sent away, but it is a beam of light bent off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraction is the bending of a light beam as it passes from one medium into another.

clue.text: Factory grade popular sort of banana

parts.note: a plant is a factory
A is a grade, as in exams
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A factory grading a well-liked banana variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy cooking banana, a variety of the fruit.

clue.text: A lot of net practice needed to make them relent with warm shaking?

definitions.text: A lot of net practice needed to make them

indicators.note: shaking stirs up the letters of the two words before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cricketers must practise in the nets a lot before a coach relents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net practice' suggests cricket nets, but these people fish with nets.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew on fishing boats spend a great deal of time working nets, so they are made by net practice.

clue.text: Dotty or Duane's poem

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
the name Duane, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A poem by either Dotty or Duane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like a name to pair with Duane, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain, so it is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Non-soft, tangy sweet medicine introduced to a listener

indicators.note: Non-soft means p, the musical sign for soft, is taken away

parts.note: a pear drop is a boiled sweet with a sharp fruity flavour

explanation.surface: A tangy, hard candy as medicine for someone listening.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical abbreviation for piano (soft), removed from PEAR DROP, a British boiled sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear drops are liquid medicine put into the ear, the listener's organ.

clue.text: A small thing, but half the dictionary is missing?

definitions.meaning: a tiny particle, the smallest unit of an element
a dictionary runs from A to Z, so if half is missing the remainder runs to the middle letter

explanation.surface: A minor matter, except that half the dictionary has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A TO M: the first half of the alphabet, as if the back half of a dictionary were lost.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiniest unit of matter, hence a very small thing.

clue.text: Check broadcast as rulers do

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: Inspect a transmission, as those in power do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals sound: REIN, to check, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch, which is what rulers do.

clue.text: Resort without worth moved where Blackpool is

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or haunt one resorts to

indicators.note: moved means the letters of worth are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside resort lacking value relocated to Blackpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' suggests Blackpool itself, but it is a snug retreat, set 'without' (around) the letters of worth 'moved'. Blackpool is a seaside resort in Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackpool lies on England's Lancashire coast, in the region of that compass direction.

clue.text: Smash hit enthralling an island republic

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece holds the other inside
smash breaks up the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A smash hit captivating a whole island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash hit' looks like a success, but 'Smash' scrambles HIT to HTI, which is 'enthralling' A and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti, sharing Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, is a Caribbean republic.

clue.text: Crank action on right of reversed container

indicators.note: on right of puts the following piece to the right of the reversed container
reversed means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
a case is a legal action

explanation.surface: Turning a lever on the right of an upside-down box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' looks like a handle to turn, but it means an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is an eccentric person, and so is a madcap or loony.

clue.text: Lecture about, say, going round Brummie's town

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes around the rest

parts.note: to rate is to scold or lecture

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so this piece wraps the next

parts.note: e.g. means for example, that is, say
Brummie is the setter, so the setter's word for self is I

explanation.surface: A Birmingham man gives a talk about his home town.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Brummie's' gives I; 'going round' and 'about' nest the pieces one inside another. Reigate is a town in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Reigate is a commuter town in Surrey, south of London.
